name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,271

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Some baht ’ats on Ilkley recalled setup for plant rotation

indicators.note: only some of the following run of letters is wanted, a part lifted from inside the words
called back, so the run is taken from right to left instead of the usual way

blocks.note: the letters running across the end of baht, through 'ats and on, into the start of Ilkley

explanation.surface: A nod to the Yorkshire song On Ilkla Moor Baht 'at, about going hatless on the moor, turned into gardening kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Baht 'at is Yorkshire dialect for without a hat. Read backwards, the run gives KLINOSTAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A klinostat is a slowly revolving apparatus that turns growing plants so gravity acts on them evenly.

clue.text: Objectively we must trail a thousand silver birds of New Caledonia

blocks.note: K is the usual abbreviation for a thousand
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
the object form of the pronoun we

explanation.surface: A grammar point about the word we, oddly attached to some silver birds.
explanation.walkthrough: Trail means come after, so the pronoun goes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The kagu is a crested, nearly flightless grey bird found only on the Pacific island group of New Caledonia.

clue.text: Agent to detain United Nations IT director

blocks.note: to intern is to confine or detain, especially in wartime
the standard abbreviation
chief information officer, the executive in charge of IT

explanation.surface: An order to have an agent hold the United Nations' head of computing.
explanation.definitionFit: An internuncio is a papal envoy ranking below a nuncio, a diplomatic representative acting for the Pope.

clue.text: Where to bath — for Marat it may be fatal

blocks.note: no letters: this says the words around it go into French, Marat's language
French où
French à
French bain

explanation.surface: Marat was famously stabbed to death in his bath, so for him the bath was where it all ended.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for Marat tells you to put the three words into French, the language of Jean-Paul Marat, killed in his bath in 1793.
explanation.definitionFit: Ouabain is a heart poison from African plants, once used on arrow tips, so a dose can be lethal.

clue.text: Creole hotpot’s core containing halved okra enjoys popularity

indicators.note: the core of something is its centre, so only the middle of hotpot is used
cut in half, so only the front half of okra is kept
holding something inside, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: the two central letters of hotpot
the first half of okra
something that enjoys popularity is in

explanation.surface: A Caribbean stew whose okra-studded centre is a hit with diners.
explanation.definitionFit: Tok Pisin is the English-based creole spoken as a national language in Papua New Guinea.

clue.text: Tough guy primarily after violence?

indicators.note: first of all, so only the opening letter of guy is used
once violence has been done to them, the letters are knocked out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of guy

explanation.surface: A wondering note on a hard man whose first aim is to start a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a thug is a tough guy who is after violence.
explanation.definitionFit: Thuggo is a slang term for a thug, a brutish man prone to fighting and intimidation.

clue.text: Assume a valley’s shape shows deposits from Alpine glaciations

blocks.note: to don is to put on or assume, like a garment
taken as written
glaciers carve valleys into a U shape

explanation.surface: A geology lesson: a U-shaped valley reveals what Alpine ice sheets left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: The Donau glaciation is the name for an early Pleistocene stage of Alpine ice advance, also used for its gravel deposits.

clue.text: Maldivian shady bar flanking Hotel Hawaii

indicators.note: standing on both sides of something, so one piece goes either side of the other

blocks.note: a dive is a disreputable bar
H in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the US postal abbreviation for Hawaii

explanation.surface: A seedy bar on either side of a Hawaiian hotel, described by an islander.
explanation.definitionFit: Dhivehi is the language of the Maldives, the Indian Ocean island nation, so it is Maldivian speech.

clue.text: Indian barber clipped collar

indicators.note: trimmed short, so the final letter is cut away

blocks.note: to collar or nail someone is to catch and arrest them

explanation.surface: A barber in India trims a customer's collar.
explanation.walkthrough: Collar is a verb here, not a shirt part; barber is the definition, and clipped fits his trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Nai is the Hindi word for a barber, the traditional caste occupation of hair-cutting in India.

clue.text: Poorly edited cuts to deselect with a mouse

indicators.note: cutting into something means entering its body, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: to unclick an item is to deselect it with a mouse button
ed. is the abbreviation for edited

explanation.surface: A complaint that a badly edited computer manual makes you deselect things with the mouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Poorly is not an anagram signal here but the definition, meaning ill. UNCLE DICK is rhyming slang: Uncle Dick rhymes with sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang: Uncle Dick stands for sick, and feeling poorly is British for being unwell.

clue.text: Golf ball no longer used in public tee area

definitions.text: Golf ball no longer used in public tee area

indicators.note: something no longer used has been dropped, so the ball comes out of the word for public

blocks.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a secret that is out is in public
O is round, so it stands for a ball
tee is how the letter T is spelt out
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A historical golf note: an old type of ball, long retired, once seen on the public tee.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the gutta was the gutta-percha golf ball of the 1800s, no longer used on any tee.
explanation.definitionFit: Gutta is short for gutta-percha, the rubbery latex from which nineteenth-century golf balls were moulded before the rubber-core era.

clue.text: With crust of silk, filling of coulis initially baked in a fish pie

indicators.note: a crust is the outer shell, so this piece is wrapped round the rest
the filling is what lies inside, so the outer letters of the next word are dropped
at the start, so only the opening letter of each following word counts

blocks.note: a silk is a King's Counsel, a senior barrister, KC
coulis without its first and last letters
first letters of baked, in and a

explanation.surface: A recipe: a silky crust over a fruit-sauce centre, baked inside a fish pie.
explanation.walkthrough: Silk is a barrister, not a fabric; KC goes round the rest as the crust.
explanation.definitionFit: Koulibiac is a Russian pastry pie filled with salmon or other fish, rice and eggs.

clue.text: Am I getting frantic with medium emergencies?

definitions.text: Am I getting frantic with medium emergencies?

indicators.note: something frantic is wild and disordered, so these letters are thrown about

blocks.note: taken as written
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium
taken as written

explanation.surface: A worried professional, pressed by a run of routine crises, wonders if they are losing their nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: someone asking whether they are getting frantic in a crisis is a nervous wreck.
explanation.definitionFit: A screaming meemie is a hysterical person, or a fit of nervous hysteria, so the panicky question describes one.

clue.text: Poorly edited with PC if supporting Mac’s earliest form of data storage

indicators.note: an edited text has been rearranged, so these letters are reordered
the earliest part is the beginning, so only the first letter of Mac's is used

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
the opening letter of Mac's

explanation.surface: A computer-war jibe: a shoddily edited PC sits underneath a Mac.
explanation.walkthrough: Poorly looks like the anagram signal, as it was at 8 Down; here it is fodder and edited does the stirring.
explanation.definitionFit: A microfloppy is the small 3.5-inch floppy disk, a removable medium for keeping computer files.

clue.text: Times in animal life, every time seeming simple

indicators.note: one thing placed in another goes inside it

blocks.note: fauna is the animal life of a region
x is the multiplication sign, read as times
if can mean whenever, every time that

explanation.surface: A naturalist's reflection on how creatures, every time, appear innocent.
explanation.definitionFit: Faux-naif describes someone affecting a childlike innocence, falsely appearing artless and unsophisticated.

clue.text: Variety of pipe down inside absurdly low roof

indicators.note: in an absurd, nonsensical manner, so the letters fall into a new order
placed within, so one piece sits in the middle of the other

blocks.note: the letters of low roof rearranged
sh is the hushing word for be quiet

explanation.surface: Someone told to be quiet under a ridiculously low ceiling, like a cramped pub with smoking pipes.
explanation.walkthrough: Pipe is a verb meaning make a noise; pipe down is the order to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A floor show is a cabaret or variety entertainment performed in a nightclub, so variety names it.

clue.text: Pickle left by escaping Soviet spy, having advanced Greek character slightly

indicators.note: what escapes gets away, so those letters leave the spy's name
moved forward, with slightly saying just one step in the alphabet, so one letter swaps for its successor

blocks.note: Kim Philby, the British intelligence officer who spied for Moscow
L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written
phi moves on one place in the Greek alphabet to the next letter
no letters: it limits the advance to a single step along the alphabet

explanation.surface: A spy-story fragment: a Soviet mole escapes, leaving behind a Greek with slightly better prospects.
explanation.walkthrough: Kim Philby defected to Moscow in 1963. Removing L and BY leaves KIM PHI, and phi becomes chi.
explanation.definitionFit: Kimchi is the Korean pickle of fermented cabbage and other vegetables seasoned with chilli.

clue.text: With loss of power, Twitter repeatedly affected

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away, so that letter goes
more than once, so the remaining chunk is written out twice

blocks.note: a cheep is a bird's twitter
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A jab at a social-media platform that loses its clout and becomes repetitive and mannered.
explanation.walkthrough: Twitter is a bird's chirp, not the website.
explanation.definitionFit: Chee-chee describes the mincing, sing-song English once attributed to Anglo-Indians, so it means mannered or affected.

clue.text: Abandoned plantation’s cover for a monstrous head?

blocks.note: a monstrous head is the head of a monster, an orc from fantasy fiction
a hat is a covering for the head

explanation.surface: A deserted plantation offers headgear for an ogre.
explanation.walkthrough: Abandoned marks the word as obsolete: orchat is an old spelling, no longer used.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchat is an obsolete form of orchard, a plantation of fruit trees, so a dropped word for one.

clue.text: One has a very light trunk in the morning collection

definitions.text: One has a very light trunk

blocks.note: a.m. stands for before noon
a batch is a set or collection

explanation.surface: Packing a featherweight suitcase for an early-morning collection.
explanation.walkthrough: Trunk looks like luggage; it is the stem of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The ambatch is an African tree of the Nile region whose pithy wood is extremely buoyant and was used for rafts.

clue.text: Black medic possibly twisting arm in traumatised state

indicators.note: twisted letters are bent out of their order
placed in something means going inside it

blocks.note: the letters of arm rearranged
shock is the state of someone traumatised

explanation.surface: A Black doctor twists an arm while someone is in shock.
explanation.walkthrough: Black medic is not a doctor: black medick is a clover-like plant, one of several claimed as the true shamrock.
explanation.definitionFit: Black medick is a trefoil sometimes sold as the Irish emblem, hence possibly as a by-example hint.

clue.text: Noah’s son turning on God yet ultimately believing in a Messiah

indicators.note: turning round sends the name back to front
in the end, so only the final letter of yet is used

blocks.note: Ham was one of Noah's three sons
Dis is the Roman god of the underworld
last letter of yet

explanation.surface: A son of Noah turning against God, yet ending up believing in a saviour.
explanation.walkthrough: Dis, the Roman god of the dead, is a common crossword god.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mahdist is a follower of the Mahdi, the redeemer whom many Muslims expect, so a believer in that messianic figure.

clue.text: Without shortening, cut a ribbon attached to a mitre

indicators.note: cut short, so the final letter is removed

blocks.note: in full means unabridged, with nothing shortened
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to trim a bishop's ribbon without trimming it, a paradox.
explanation.definitionFit: An infula is one of the two lappets or fringed bands hanging from the back of a bishop's mitre.

clue.text: Changing hormone can help with front of brain or its hind part

indicators.note: a change of arrangement, so these letters are reordered
the front is the start, so just the first letter of brain

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the first letter of brain

explanation.surface: A medical claim that a hormone treatment can help the front of the brain or the back.
explanation.walkthrough: Front of brain looks like part of the definition; it is only the B, and its hind part is the definition, its meaning the brain's.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhombencephalon is the hindbrain, the rearmost of the three primary regions of the developing vertebrate brain.

clue.text: Radioactive gas no longer standing out, apparently

indicators.note: in a down entry, standing up means reading from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: out is not in

explanation.surface: A gas that no longer stands out, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: No longer marks a superseded name, part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Niton was an early name for the element now called radon, the heavy radioactive noble gas, since dropped.

clue.text: Hard to feed heavy demand I didn’t hear about — it’s up to Joshua

indicators.note: turned about, so the run of pieces before it faces the other way

blocks.note: in the theatre, to feed an actor a line is to give a cue
a tax is a burdensome demand
eh? is what you say when you did not catch something
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone struggling to meet a heavy, half-heard demand, then a sudden aside about the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: Feed is a stage term: the feed or straight man gives the comic a cue. Only the three pieces after Hard are turned about, and H is added to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hexateuch is the first six books of the Old Testament, Genesis through to the Book of Joshua, read as a unit.

clue.text: Steer around right circuit

indicators.note: turned around, so the word faces the other way

blocks.note: a steer is a castrated bullock, an ox
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Driving instructions: steer around and go right at the roundabout.
explanation.walkthrough: Steer is a noun here, the animal, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: XOR is the exclusive-or logic gate, an electronic circuit giving output when exactly one input is true.

clue.text: Punishing task of writing is the author’s bag

blocks.note: the author is I, and I'm is short for I am, standing for the author is
to bag game is to pot it, shoot it

explanation.surface: A writer's confession that a punitive writing chore is very much their thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Bag means kill or capture, so pot as in pot-shot; the author is the setter, I.
explanation.definitionFit: An impot is school slang for an imposition, lines a pupil is made to write out as punishment.

clue.text: Hardie’s bland answers had less fringe material

indicators.note: material with no fringe is only the inner stuff, so the answer sits within the words

blocks.note: the run across the end of answers and the start of had

explanation.surface: Keir Hardie's dull replies had less frill to them.
explanation.walkthrough: Keir Hardie was the Scottish founder of the Labour Party, so his word is a Scots one.
explanation.definitionFit: Wersh is Scots for tasteless or insipid, so a Scotsman's word for bland or flavourless.

clue.text: Bitter cold stress applied to subtropical tree

blocks.note: bitter is a type of beer, ale
C for cold, as on a tap
to try someone is to strain or stress them
on can mean placed upon, applied to

explanation.surface: A sharp cold snap putting pressure on a warm-climate tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a kind of British beer, not a sense of cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Alectryon is a genus of trees and shrubs of the soapberry family native to warm regions of Australasia and the Pacific.
